Rigid lorries

Category C training

Practical training for rigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, for drivers moving up from a car licence.

In plain English

Category C is the rigid lorry entitlement. It covers goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes maximum authorised mass that are not articulated. Training is the practical preparation for that test: the vehicle, the manoeuvres and the road driving.

Who it is for

People who want to drive a rigid goods vehicle over 3.5 tonnes. A category B car licence is the usual starting point. Medical and theory steps sit alongside the practical training.

What it covers

  • Rigid goods vehicles such as box wagons, tippers, flatbeds and similar lorries
  • Not an articulated lorry or a drawbar outfit. That is Category C+E

Training takes place in a rigid goods vehicle suited to the Category C practical test.

Eligibility and prerequisites

A general guide. We check your own licence when you enquire.

  • A category B car licence is the usual starting point
  • A medical assessment is normally required before a lorry practical test
  • Theory tests sit alongside the time in the vehicle
  • Paid driving work can also require Driver CPC, which is a separate qualification
  • Age and medical requirements depend on the individual and the work, so we check these with you when you enquire

What the training includes

  • Familiarisation with a rigid goods vehicle
  • Reversing and off-road manoeuvres
  • On-road driving
  • Guidance on what the practical test involves

How the course works

  1. Enquire about Category C

    Say which course you want, which base you prefer, and how you would like to be contacted.

  2. Check the licence you hold

    We check the entitlement you hold before training is arranged, so the plan fits your starting point.

  3. Train in the vehicle

    Practical time covers the vehicle, the manoeuvres and the road driving.

  4. Prepare for the practical test

    We explain how the test is booked when you enquire, and what to expect on the day.

Training format

Yard work and road driving, run from each base that offers Category C. We agree dates with you when you enquire.

Duration and cost

How long training takes depends on the licence you already hold and your experience in this type of vehicle. We confirm it when you enquire.

We quote once we know the licence you hold and the training you need. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate costs where they apply.

Questions about this course

What does Category C allow me to drive?

Rigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes. It does not cover an articulated lorry or a drawbar trailer. That is Category C+E.

How long does Category C take, and what does it cost?

How long Category C takes depends on your starting point, and the fee depends on the training you need. We confirm both when you enquire. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate costs.
